title: The Clayton-Bulwer treaty of 1850 is about a ship canal between the Atlantic and the Pacific
summary: The 1850 Clayton-Bulwer treaty concerns a proposed Atlantic-Pacific ship canal through Nicaragua.
body: The Clayton-Bulwer treaty addresses a ship canal between the Atlantic and Pacific by way of the San Juan River and the lakes of Nicaragua. Britain and the United States agree about a Central American canal neither of them then built on that route. The later Panama treaty is a different instrument. The wording on the page includes: "any persons or company should already have, with any State through which the proposed ship canal may pass, a contract for the construction of such a canal as that specified in this convention, to the stipulations of which contract neither of the contracting parties in this convention have any just cause to object, and the said persons or company shall".
said_by: United States and Great Britain, Avalon Project
